posts.cooked:
I downloaded d backup of my Shopify Product catalog with 313 independent listings with multiple product images & variants for each listing.

When I attempted to restore this backup file (that Shopify PROVIDED)- NONE of the additional images, variant images or inventory values would re-populate.

When I look at the .csv file- ALL of the image urls/inventory data and information are present. However, when I re-upload that file- Shopify simply publishes ONE single product image (omitting all the rest that attached to that listing)- NONE of the supplemental listing images/videos. NONE of the variant images. NONE of the variant inventory data.

My store has been down for 3 days now with ZERO support from Shopify who claims to be “re-indexing” the .csv file. Thus far- nothing has worked.

This is an INSANE misstep on Shopify’s side to deliver a backup file that they themselves cannot honor or restore completely. I have no clue how to proceed and am in absolute distress ad I cannot re-do all of my inventory or manually update ALL of my listings by hand.
That’s very unfortunate @HUNTEDFOX , I’m sorry. Would you be ok with sharing the first 10-20 rows of the file so I can take a look at it and see if I can figure what’s going on?

I have been on “support” chat with Shopify for DAYS now- and here is what I have discovered:

I replaced my products with an import that eliminated all of my variants and supplemental product images.

When I uploaded the backup .csv- Shopify failed to and continues to fail to acknowledge and apply the image files in column AB (of their own backup file) which points to all of the files that are stored in the content->files section of Shopify.

FURTHERMORE- and even more devastating is that column T states that inventory is managed by Shopify.

SO- when all of the variants were deleted and failed to restore- Shopify eliminated ALL OF MY INVENTORY DATA including qty/location.

I had NO idea that this could possibly be the result when i downloaded a BACKUP of my entire product catalog as per Shopify’s own instructions.

My entire store is dismantled and my e-commerce is absolutely stopped as a result of this.

Hi @HUNTEDFOX — your post about trying to restore 313 listings from Shopify’s own backup CSV, and losing the variant images and inventory, stuck with me.

I’m honest upfront: I’m researching before building anything. I have an idea for a small CSV-checking tool for Shopify merchants, but there is no product yet — nothing to buy, and I’m not selling anything.

Would you be open to a 15-minute chat about how you import / update products, and the last time a CSV import went wrong? I just want to learn what’s actually painful, so I don’t build the wrong thing.

Happy to work around your timezone, voice or text — whichever is easier. And if it’s useful, I can share a short summary of what I hear from other merchants (anonymised) once I’ve done a few chats.

If not, no worries at all — thanks for reading.

The most likely cause is not that the data is missing from the file. It is that a Shopify product export is a catalog snapshot, not a full restore file, and the import rules for variants, extra images, and inventory are different from what the export shows.

1. Variants and extra images only come back if the rows are grouped exactly. Every row for one product must share the exact same Handle, and every continuation row must leave Title blank. If a Handle is changed, even by a hyphen or a space, or if Title is repeated on the variant rows, Shopify creates separate products instead of one product with variants. Check that first, because that alone explains variants disappearing.

2. Extra images need their own rows. The first image goes on the main product row. Each additional image must be on its own row with the same Handle, Title blank, and only the Image Src and Image Position filled in. An Image Src that is a page link, a file that needs a login, or a video file will not import as a product image. Image Src must be a direct public http or https link to the image file itself. Product videos are not restored by a product CSV at all. They have to be uploaded again in the product editor.

3. Inventory is the trap in this file. If Variant Inventory Tracker is blank or not set to shopify, Shopify will not track or restore stock for that variant. Also, a product import on its own is not a reliable way to restore quantities by location. Restore stock separately with an inventory import, which has a location column, and confirm the location name in the file matches the location in your store exactly.

4. Do not re-import the whole 313-product file again until a test works. Take one product that lost its variants and images, copy only its rows into a small test file, tick Overwrite products with matching handles, and import that one product. If the test product comes back complete, the problem was grouping or the Overwrite setting on the full import, and you can safely repeat it for the rest. If the test product still comes back with only one image, check the Image Src values in that test file first, because that is where the break is.

Also, before another full import, export what is currently in the store and keep it aside. Re-importing without Overwrite checked will not replace the damaged products, and re-importing with it checked will replace them with whatever is in the file, so you want a copy of the current state first.

ai_summary.summarized_text:
A merchant’s Shopify store was left unusable after a product CSV import failed to restore variants, additional product and variant images, and inventory for 313 listings. Although the exported file appeared to contain the relevant data, Shopify reportedly restored only one image per product and did not restore stock quantities; support had not resolved the issue after several days.

A reply suggested that a Shopify product export may not function as a complete backup, and that import formatting and settings could explain the missing data. The advice was to check that product rows share the same Handle and continuation rows leave Title blank; additional images need separate rows with direct, publicly accessible image URLs. Product videos cannot be restored through the product CSV. Inventory quantities, particularly by location, may need a separate inventory import with matching location names and Shopify selected as the inventory tracker.

Before retrying the full catalog, the merchant was advised to save the current store state and test one product with matching handles and overwrite enabled. No successful recovery or final resolution was reported.
